cells.evidence: 3,000 attempts, 38 accepted, 2,962 duplicate-hash rejections and zero band-mismatch. The generator's candidates were 98.7% puzzles already in the corpus, so the space of band-1 4x4 puzzles with diagonal symmetry is essentially full at 43 records.

3,000 attempts, 15 accepted, 2,985 duplicate-hash rejections and zero band-mismatch. Capacity varies sharply by symmetry at this shape: diagonal holds 43, mirror_h only 15, because a horizontal mirror constrains a 4x4 clue pattern much harder.

3,000 attempts, 5 accepted, 2,995 duplicate-hash rejections and zero band-mismatch. This cell has a closed-form ceiling rather than an empirical one: rot90 partitions a 4x4's 16 cells into exactly 4 orbits of 4, so a rot90-symmetric clue pattern is a union of orbits and there are only 2^4 - 1 = 15 non-empty patterns in total. Every accepted record has 8 clues, i.e. exactly 2 of the 4 orbits, and the corpus holds 4 of the 6 possible two-orbit patterns. One orbit (4 clues) cannot force a unique solution and three (12 clues) does not reach band 1, so 8 clues is the only workable size. rot90 is offered at band 1 only, so this is the whole 4x4 rot90 space.
